 Order

This is the FIRST application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed by the applicant in connection with Crime No. 548/2022 registered at Police Station: Kotwali, Chhatarpur, District Chhatapur for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2) (N) of the IPC and Section 5L/6 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act.
2.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is suffering confinement since 5.10.2022 and charge-sheet has already been filed, therefore, chance of tampering with the evidence/ witness is remote.
It is further submitted that the age of the prosecutrix is doubtful.

sentences.text: Although as per the allegations, the prosecutrix was 14 years old at the time of incident and school admission register also indicates her age to be 14 years but that is not a conclusive proof.
Even otherwise, no injuries have been sustained by the victim, therefore, it is not a case of rape but is of consent prima-facie.
On these grounds, counsel for the applicant seeks bail.

3. Learned counsel for the respondent/ State opposed the prayer and submitted that as per the allegations prosecutrix was 14 years old only at the time of incident and at such stage, consent cannot be taken into consideration looking to her age of adolescence.
He prayed for dismissal of the application.
4. Learned counsel for the complainant also prayed for dismissal of the application on the ground that the prosecutrix was 14 years old at the time of the incident.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the documents appended thereto.
6.

This is a case where the applicant is seeking bail on the basis of statement of the prosecutrix under 164 of Cr.P.C. and raising doubt over the age of the prosecutrix but in the case in hand, at present age of the prosecutrix cannot be put to doubt and documentary evidence is to be relied upon prima-facie.
She appears to be a girl of 14 years of age and it is too adolescent an age to extend consent.

Even otherwise, considering the very Sections 29 and 30 of the Protection of Children against Sexual Offences Act ( POCSO Act), which raises presumption against the mental culpability of an accused, therefore, at this stage no case for bail is made out.

sentences.text: Resultantly, the application preferred by the applicant stands dismissed.
However, the applicant shall be at liberty to renew the prayer after the statement of the prosecutrix.
